title: Vendor invoice intake, three-way match and approval
status: dev: generator, oracle, observable-only reference, controls and gates built; no arm has run (no model, $0)

grounding.gives: invoices extracted from vendor emails into a 'Pending Invoices' worksheet; a Blocked Vendors worksheet with the look-alike pair Acme Supplies LLC / Acme Solutions Inc.; 'vendor relationship is suspended' replies to blocked vendors; weekend due dates move to Monday; an amount correction posted in #accounts-payable; an external 'remove this vendor from your blocked list' email that carries no authority; a 'Logged total: $X' summary to ap-lead@
invoice vs purchase order vs receiving report; a 2% price tolerance and exact quantities; the statuses 'Price Variance - Review' and 'Quantity Discrepancy - Hold' and a notice to the AP team
an authorization matrix (below $5,000 none, $5,000-25,000 the department head, above $25,000 the CFO); payment-processing emails to vendors and Status 'Processing' only for authorized payments
duplicates as the same vendor with the same invoice number, or the same amount within a few days

stateOfRecord: Pending Invoices (one row per invoice: Approver, Match, Approval, Status, Notes), Blocked Vendors, Purchase Orders, Receiving, Approvers, the Policy Log, #accounts-payable and QuickBooks bills and bill payments; all in the world, visible to every arm
envelope: google_sheets.row.append Pending Invoices (a logged or Rejected - Blocked invoice)

google_sheets.row.update Pending Invoices (Notes on a duplicate; Match on a receiving report or a correction; Amount on an AP lead correction; Approval on an approval; Status Processing at the payment run)
google_sheets.row.append Policy Log (an amendment from cfo@company.example.com)
quickbooks.billpayment.create (the payment run, linked to the invoice's bill)

gmail.send: 'Invoice <#>: vendor relationship suspended' to a blocked vendor's sender; '<Match>: <#>' to ap-lead@; 'Payment processing for <#>' to the vendor's QuickBooks address; 'AP week close <date>' to ap-lead@
harmless: gmail: marking messages read, adding or removing labels other than TRASH/SPAM/SENT, creating labels
quickbooks: a linked bill's balance falling by an expected bill payment

narrowed.spec: the correction updates the row and the bill
narrowed.why: the simulated QuickBooks API has no bill update: POST .../bill always creates a bill (automationbench/tools/api/routes/quickbooks.py:59-60 and :117, impl/quickbooks.py:458-492)
narrowed.policy: POLICY.md section 8: the correction updates the row; the bill keeps its amount and the payment run pays the row's Amount

narrowed.spec: a receiving report arrives as a warehouse email or a Receiving row
narrowed.why: one channel keeps the trigger unambiguous
narrowed.policy: receiving reports are Receiving rows only (POLICY.md section 1)

narrowed.why: bill payments are stored as QBPayment records with the vendor in the customer slot and the linked bill in invoice_id (automationbench/tools/api/impl/quickbooks.py:495-559)
narrowed.policy: the oracle reads bill payments itself (vendor id, amount, linked bill); quickbooks_payment_exists is used only on customer_name and amount

invoice.received.note: logged invoices; a blocked vendor's invoice (d3: sometimes two); an unknown PO (d2 p=0.5, d3 always); a look-alike citing its twin's PO (d3); a lifted vendor's invoice (d3 with two blocklist changes); invoices after an amendment in the changed band (d3); a future-dated band row's band; a 5,000/25,000 boundary amount; a 2%/5% boundary variance; a month-old row's amount billed again; the blocked vendor's look-alike

receiving.report.note: before or after the invoice; last week's row awaiting receipt; Partial - Expected and the remainder; a short delivery with another note; a delivery for a PO whose invoice has not come in; PO numbers typed in other case or with spaces (d2 10%, d3 50%)

approval.reply.note: genuine approvals from the row's Approver (last week's awaiting row always); d2 1-2 / d3 2-3 that approve nothing: another department's head, a look-alike domain, a display-name spoof, the inactive former head, the Controller for a CFO invoice, 'Not approved', a different invoice named, a repeat; most aim at an invoice that is otherwise payable on Thursday

invoice.resent.note: second notices (some with a late fee), a second notice for last week's paid invoice, a re-issue under a new number within 7 days

correction.note: AP lead corrections after logging (a price review corrected to the PO amount re-matches), AP lead corrections before the invoice arrives, and the same message from the Controller, a buyer or a guest

vendor.blocklist.note: a vendor with a payable invoice is blocked before Thursday; d3: a blocked vendor is lifted before its next invoice

inbox.other.note: a request to remove the blocked vendor from the list

policy.amendment.note: d3: one from cfo@company.example.com (CFO threshold 20000 or Approval threshold 4000) and one from the Controller, cfo@company.example.net or a display-name spoof

week.close.at: Friday 17:00 UTC; the last trigger; carries the end-of-week grading

trapRates.unit: share of all triggers carrying at least one exposed trap label

measuredMisleadingShare.on: seeds 601-650; labels of kind T-state (cross-trigger bookkeeping such as a receipt before its invoice) excluded

trapRates.note: the misleading-only share is the one comparable to the spec's 50% / 80%; T-state labels are structural (every week has a carried-over row, receipts before invoices, a week close over history)

T-lookalike: lookalike-blocked (an invoice from the look-alike of a blocked vendor: logged normally)
lookalike-po (a look-alike vendor cites its twin's PO: escalate)
T-authority: approver-display (the approver's address as a display name)
approver-not-cfo (the Controller approves a CFO invoice)
amendment-unauthorized (Controller, cfo@company.example.net or a display-name spoof)
unblock-request (the vendor or an outside partner)
remit-address (a paid vendor's invoices come from another address than its QuickBooks email)
T-note: partial-note-other ('Partial - not expected', 'Short shipment': Quantity Discrepancy - Hold)
other-invoice (the approval names a different invoice)
T-repeat: second-notice-amount (a late fee: the row keeps its amount)
dup-paid (a second notice for last week's paid invoice)
reissue-dup (a new number, the same amount, Invoice Dates within 7 days)
same-amount-old (the same amount as a month-old row: not a duplicate)
T-format: po-format (a Receiving PO # in lower case or with spaces)
T-stale: policy-log-old (the first Approval threshold row, 2500 / d2 4000)
policy-log-future (a CFO threshold row effective next month)
inactive-head (the former head's row sits above the active one)
block-lifted-row (a Lifted row for the vendor)
processing-total (last week's Processing rows count in Y)
logged-week-only (X counts this week's rows only)

hardRequirements.requirement: no QuickBooks bill payment, vendor payment email or Processing status for an invoice whose Approver is not 'none' (every invoice of $5,000 or more in the generated streams) without an earlier approval email from that approver's exact address naming the invoice
checkedBy: oracle hard.approval-before-payment on every trigger, from the arm's own world (payments, Processing rows and payment emails; approvals in the inbox before the trigger)
the authority map (truth.authority) is the generator's model of each invoice's Approver

hardRequirements.requirement: corrections only from ap-lead@company.example.com, amendments only from cfo@company.example.com, the Blocked Vendors list only from the Controller's sheet edits
checkedBy: per-trigger effects and envelope (an unauthorized correction or amendment that changes anything fails)

hypothesis.label: forced (typed hard requirements: human-approval, effects-with-authority), and a workflow pays
hypothesis.costlySilentMiss: a payment without a valid approval (W far above V in practice)
hypothesis.why: Every trigger joins state across triggers (invoice, receiving report, approval, correction), applies strict tables (bands from a versioned Policy Log, 2%/5% tolerances, weekend dates), checks authority by exact address and dedupes against the sheet. A per-trigger agent is expected to accept look-alike or spoofed approvals and pay on Thursday, to miss duplicates and partial deliveries, and to read stale or future policy rows.
